flow_guide._about: Flow bands by craft at USGS 09497500 (Salt River near Chrysotile, at the put-in), compiled 2026-11-13 from American Whitewater, Mild to Wild, cacreeks, Riverbrain and Williams' Paddling Arizona; raft bands set by the site owner. 'range' is the default 'your range' on Seasonal flows: every band from the first runnable one to the last before experts-only.

bands.label: Too low
bands.note: Too low for loaded rafts; day-trip rafts need about 500 cfs. Black Rock is unrunnable at 500-600 cfs and below.

bands.label: Bony
bands.note: Scrapey. With bigger rafts, consider launching at Camp 5 instead of Camp 1. Avoid Island Rapid below 1,200 cfs.

bands.label: Solid flow
bands.note: 1,200 cfs is American Whitewater's recommended minimum for gear-hauling rafts.

bands.label: Ideal
bands.note: Class III pool-drop with Class IV in the lower gorges.

bands.label: Fast
bands.note: Big wave trains and more rapids at Class IV; little time to recover between drops.

bands.label: High: experts only
bands.note: Huge waves, several IV+ rapids, Cibecue Creek hard to cross, flood risk.

bands.label: Too low
bands.note: Below the published minimums for inflatable kayaks and packrafts.

bands.label: Low, technical
bands.note: Scraping and some walking; Black Rock is often walked.

bands.label: Good
bands.note: American Whitewater: rapids are enjoyable down to about 400 cfs for kayaks and packrafts.

bands.label: Pushy
bands.note: Class IV in the lower gorges; strong skills needed.

bands.label: Experts with a roll only
bands.note: A self-support ducky party at about 5,000 cfs did not recommend it to anyone without a roll.

flow_guide.notes: Flows usually drop during a trip, so check the whole trip, not just launch day. Low water makes some rapids harder, not easier: at low water a few approach Class V. Cibecue, Canyon and Cherry creeks add water below the gauge.

Tonto NF: Salt River Canyon Wilderness

summary: A Tonto National Forest permit, won in a winter lottery, is required to float the Salt River Canyon Wilderness from March 1 to May 15. A separate White Mountain Apache Tribe recreation permit is required for the reservation stretch below the Highway 60 put-in.

permits.name: Salt River Canyon Wilderness permit
permits.when: Required March 1 to May 15 each year
permits.how: Lottery on Recreation.gov, December 1 to January 31. One application per person.
permits.cost: $125 per permit, due by February 20 after the drawing

permits.name: White Mountain Apache Tribe recreation permit
permits.when: Required for about 29 miles downstream of First Campground and the Highway 60 bridge put-in
permits.how: Buy from the Tribe's outdoor recreation office. Print it or save it to your phone: there is no cell service at the put-in.
permits.cost: Check current fees with the Tribe

rules: Permit holder must be 18 or older and must organize a non-commercial trip. No commercial use by participants.
Launch on your permitted date. Carry the signed permit; every person carries a valid photo ID.
Fire pan with sides at least 3 inches high. Self-support kayak trips may use a fire blanket instead.
Portable toilet system for all solid human waste; carry it all out of the river corridor.
No motorized equipment or motorboats in the wilderness.
Whitewater boating is prohibited by the Tribe upstream of Apache Falls, a quarter mile above the Highway 60 bridge.
Cancel at least 21 days before launch for a refund. Cancelled dates go back on Recreation.gov at a random time within 24 hours.
open_questions: Lottery results date is not published on the Forest Service page.
Whether a San Carlos Apache Tribe permit is also needed on river left; confirm with both tribes.
